newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon economy improves slightly in April.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon economy improves slightly in April.

text.p: Lebanon's economic activity picked up slightly in April, reaching its highest level in five months but construction remained at a lower level than a year ago, the Bank of Lebanon said on Tuesday.
The bank's coincident indicator of economic activity rose to 170.3 from 166.0 in March and well above last April's 150.1 when Israel launched a 17-day blitz on Lebanon that caused widespread damage.
"The BDL coincident indicator suggests a slight pick-up in economic activity, in part seasonal," the central bank said in its latest monthly economic report.
"Construction activity continued its downward trend suffering from market disequilibrium and housing loan scarcity," it added.

The indicator combines 12 economic series including imports, exports, electricity output and airport and port activity. The bank has not revealed the weighting of the different series and some economists question its value.
Industrial investment remained subdued in April with imports of industrial equipment falling 90.1 percent on a year-on-year basis.
"The levels recorded during April 1996 were exceptionally high because cement companies imported machines to upgrade their capacities," the bulletin said.
The balance of payments registered a "seasonal deficit" of $45.7 million in April compared with a $103.2 million shortfall a year earlier.
This brought the balance of payments surplus for the first four months of the year to $517 million.
"This deficit is reflected in a decline in the net foreign assets of commercial banks by $143.2 million while foreign assets of the central bank rose by $95.7 million," the bank said.
